=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py
Line or code reference: _run_snapshot_for_cache (line ~248 in diff)
Problem: _run_snapshot_for_cache creates lightweight cache snapshots without cost_telemetry. The rows_snapshot at line 1441, initially populated from collected_rows_for_repo which may carry cost_telemetry from the previous run s cache, gets overwritten by updated_rows at line 1516 during the log-fetch phase. This is correct in steady state, but on the very first run after deployment, cost_telemetry enters the cache for a run only after the log-fetch loop at line 1482 completes. Any other concurrent path that reads the cache before the log-fetch phase finishes on the initial run could see rows without cost_telemetry. In practice this is self-healing and transient, and the aggregate_run_cost_telemetry function already filters runs without cost_telemetry (log_parsed is not True), so aggregate values would simply undercount during the first collection cycle. This is acceptable fail-open behavior, not a crash.
Why it fails at runtime: Aggregate cost_telemetry values undercount runs on the very first collection cycle post-deployment.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- File: scripts/analyze_workflow_logs.py
Line or code reference: prepare_analysis_context, line 315-316
Problem: summary["cost_telemetry"] is unconditionally overwritten with aggregate_run_cost_telemetry(runs) after dict(summary) creates a shallow copy. When summary already carries cost_telemetry from the collector s build_report or from _summarize_runs, this line recomputes the same aggregate from the same runs list. The overwrite is redundant rather than divergent — both the collector and the analyzer use the same aggregate_run_cost_telemetry function on the same runs list, producing identical output. The per_repo and per_workflow_family else blocks at lines 338-354 patching cost_telemetry into entries follow the same pattern: _aggregate_runs_by_key already computes cost_telemetry over group-scoped rows matching the current runs, so the overlay replaces with equivalent values. No actual data divergence occurs in the current data flow.
Why it fails at runtime: It does not fail at runtime. The redundant recomputation wastes CPU but produces correct results.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- File: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py
Line or code reference: main function, the removal of the log_archive_cache is not None guard, line ~1482
Problem: The old code had a fallback path calling list_run_log_excerpts when log_archive_cache was None. The new code unconditionally calls _fetch_run_log_archive(repository, run_id, token=token, cache=log_archive_cache). When log_archive_cache is None, _fetch_run_log_archive handles it gracefully (the cache parameter defaults to None and the function body checks isinstance(cache, dict)). The new code always downloads the full log archive via extract_full_logs which reads complete step logs, whereas the old code used extract_log_excerpts which only reads the first 16KB per step. This is a necessary tradeoff for cost_telemetry parsing which needs full logs. The API endpoint is the same; the difference is in how much data is decompressed from the zip archive. The try/except catches any failures and logs them.
Why it fails at runtime: It does not fail at runtime. Full-log reading is needed for the cost-telemetry feature.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- File: scripts/analyze_workflow_logs.py
Line or code reference: _aggregate_runs_by_key, line ~260
Problem: The function now accumulates full run dicts in entry["rows"] for each key group, then pops them to compute cost_telemetry via aggregate_run_cost_telemetry. For runs that carry log_excerpts and cost_telemetry dicts, this doubles the in-memory representation during the aggregation phase. For a collection run covering many repositories with thousands of workflow runs, this could increase peak memory usage. However, the runs are already fully loaded in memory by the caller, and the cost_telemetry dicts are small metadata. The rows list is popped and garbage-collected after each key group is processed, so the additional memory is temporary and bounded by the largest group size.
Why it fails at runtime: Does not fail at runtime but could cause higher memory pressure on very large collections. Mitigated by group-level processing and pop + GC.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

- File: scripts/cost_audit.py
Line or code reference: _to_int / _to_float function promotion (line ~164)
Problem: The _to_int helper function was promoted from a local closure inside parse_log to a module-level function. The original local _to_int inside parse_log has been removed, and all call sites (including parse_log itself) now use the module-level _to_int. The function signature changed from def _to_int(v: str) -> int (local, accepting only strings) to def _to_int(value: Any, default: int = 0) -> int (module-level, accepting Any with a default). This is a superset of the old behavior and does not break any callers. The old local function was scoped inside parse_log and was never externally accessible.
Why it fails at runtime: Does not fail at runtime. The new function is a superset; existing tests for parse_log in test_cost_audit_semble_metrics.py pass.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1
